content: For the treatment of active duodenal ulcers in adults, the recommended oral dose of Famotidine is 40 mg taken once daily at bedtime. Most patients achieve healing within four weeks, and it is rarely necessary to continue the full dosage for more than six to eight weeks. Alternatively, a regimen of 20 mg taken twice daily is also effective. For maintenance therapy, the recommended dose is 20 mg taken once daily at bedtime. For the treatment of active benign gastric ulcers in adults, the recommended oral dose of Famotidine is 40 mg taken once daily at bedtime. For adult patients with symptoms of gastroesophageal reflux disease (GERD), the recommended oral dose is 20 mg taken twice daily for up to six weeks. For those with esophagitis, including erosions and ulcerations associated with GERD, the recommended dose is 20 mg or 40 mg taken twice daily for up to 12 weeks. In pediatric patients under one year of age with GERD, the suggested starting dose of Famotidine oral suspension is 0.5 mg/kg per dose. For infants under three months of age, this dose is administered once daily for up to eight weeks. For infants aged three months to less than one year, the dose is given twice daily. The use of intravenous Famotidine in this age group has not been adequately studied. For pediatric patients aged one to 16 years, the suggested starting doses are as follows: For peptic ulcers: 0.5 mg/kg/day taken orally at bedtime or divided into two doses, up to a maximum of 40 mg/day. For GERD, with or without esophagitis, including erosions and ulcerations: 1.0 mg/kg/day taken orally in two divided doses, up to a maximum of 40 mg twice daily. While uncontrolled studies suggest Famotidine may be effective for these conditions in pediatric patients, data are insufficient to establish precise response rates based on dose and duration. Published studies in pediatric patients have used doses up to 1 mg/kg/day for peptic ulcers and up to 2 mg/kg/day for GERD with or without esophagitis. For patients with pathological hypersecretory conditions, such as Zollinger-Ellison Syndrome, the dosage of Famotidine should be individualized. The recommended starting dose for adults is 20 mg taken every six hours. In some cases, higher starting doses may be necessary. Dosages should be adjusted based on the patient’s clinical needs and continued as long as required. In severe cases, doses up to 160 mg every six hours have been administered. Famotidine oral suspension can be used as a substitute for Famotidine tablets for any of the above indications. Famotidine orally disintegrating tablets can also be substituted for Famotidine tablets at the same recommended dosages for any of the above indications. If needed, antacids may be administered concurrently with Famotidine. In adult patients with moderate renal insufficiency (creatinine clearance <50 mL/min) or severe renal insufficiency (creatinine clearance <10 mL/min), the elimination half-life of Famotidine is prolonged. In patients with severe renal insufficiency, the half-life may exceed 20 hours, reaching approximately 24 hours in anuric patients. To prevent excessive drug accumulation and potential central nervous system side effects, the dose of Famotidine may be reduced to half the usual dose, or the dosing interval may be extended to 36 to 48 hours, depending on the patient’s clinical response. Dosage adjustments should also be considered for pediatric patients with moderate or severe renal insufficiency, based on pharmacokinetic comparisons between adults and children.
